title: SPOOK: Sparse Pixel Optimization for Off-Manifold Knowledge in Vision Encoders
abstract: arXiv:2610.32835v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Modern vision encoders are widely used as semantic representations, but the relationship between embedding similarity and human-visible semantics can become unclear far from the natural-image manifold. We probe this regime in a black-box setting by applying sparse pixel edits to blank canvases with a simple pixel-level hill-climbing procedure. Across ImageNet and Flickr30k, we evaluate whether these edited blank canvases can retrieve chosen targets in multimodal contrastive encoders and self-supervised visual encoders. On OpenCLIP, inputs optimized toward class prompts achieve strong top-1 and top-5 targeted retrieval performance; on DINOv3, inputs optimized toward class prototypes achieve high target alignment and near-top prototype ranks. These results show that sparse edits on otherwise blank, visually non-semantic inputs can enter target semantic basins in both language-aligned and self-supervised visual representation spaces. Our

translated_title: SPOOK：视觉编码器中流形外知识的稀疏像素优化
translated_abstract: 现代视觉编码器被广泛用作语义表示，但在远离自然图像流形的区域，嵌入相似性与人类可见语义之间的关系可能变得不清晰。我们在黑盒设置下探究这一区域，通过对空白画布应用稀疏像素编辑，并采用一种简单的像素级爬山过程。在ImageNet和Flickr30k数据集上，我们评估了这些编辑过的空白画布能否在多模态对比编码器和自监督视觉编码器中检索到选定的目标。在OpenCLIP上，朝类别提示优化的输入实现了强大的top-1和top-5目标检索性能；在DINOv3上，朝类别原型优化的输入实现了高目标对齐和接近顶部的原型排名。这些结果表明，在原本空白、视觉上无语义的输入上进行稀疏编辑，即可进入语言对齐和自监督视觉表示空间中的目标语义盆地。
tldr: 该研究提出SPOOK方法，证明仅通过黑盒爬山优化对空白画布进行稀疏像素编辑，就能在OpenCLIP和DINOv3等视觉编码器的表示空间中成功检索到目标语义，揭示了远离自然图像流形处嵌入相似性与人类可见语义的脱节。
en_tdlr: SPOOK shows that sparse pixel edits on blank canvases, optimized via simple black-box hill-climbing, can enter target semantic basins in both multimodal contrastive (OpenCLIP) and self-supervised (DINOv3) vision encoders, revealing that embedding similarity diverges from human-visible semantics far off the natural-image manifold.
